result.summary: The environment is a typical urban side street with a significant lack of pedestrian-specific infrastructure at the intersection. While sidewalks are present, there are no marked crosswalks, curb ramps, or traffic control devices to protect pedestrians crossing the roadway.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted markings to indicate a pedestrian crossing area at the intersection.

hazards.name: Blind Corner
hazards.description: The brick building on the right is built right up to the sidewalk, creating a sightline obstruction for pedestrians and drivers turning the corner.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image at the building corner

hazards.name: Lack of ADA Accessibility
hazards.description: The absence of curb ramps makes the crossing difficult or impossible for people with mobility devices.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk on the right

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style painted crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install ADA-compliant curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces at all crossing points.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The street environment is characterized by an industrial setting with narrow sidewalks and a complete absence of marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming features. A vehicle is parked directly on the sidewalk area, creating a physical obstruction that would force pedestrians into the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: No designated crossing points are visible for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven road surface presents tripping hazards.

interventions.title: Street Trees

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a sidewalk that is significantly obstructed by a utility pole at the corner. There are no marked crosswalks or ADA-compliant curb ramps at this intersection, and the sidewalk pavement is in fair to poor condition.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large utility pole is located directly in the path of the sidewalk at the corner, forcing pedestrians into the street or onto unpaved ground.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crosswalk
hazards.description: No painted crosswalks are visible at the intersection, reducing driver awareness of potential pedestrians.

hazards.name: Poor Sidewalk Condition
hazards.description: The sidewalk surface is cracked and uneven, creating a tripping hazard.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Paint continental-style crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at the corner for accessibility.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Realignment or Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Relocate the utility pole or widen the sidewalk to ensure a continuous, unobstructed clear path.

result.summary: The image shows a residential/mixed-use street intersection that lacks basic pedestrian safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or traffic control signals. While sidewalks are present on both sides, the wide, unmarked roadway and parked vehicles near the corner create potential hazards for crossing pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: No painted crosswalks are visible at the intersection, providing no designated space or priority for pedestrians to cross.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the right curb may block the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street near the intersection
